message:
dana: heads up - SI partner Nimbus reported several hourly usage files where the usage_timestamp is 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. customers missing credits. :grimacing:

tom: wow okay. is that a zero-timestamp sentinel or parse error? can you paste a sample?

dana: sanitized example they sent:

```
{"partner":"nimbus","device":"n-42","usage_timestamp":"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z","meter":"compute","units":30}
```

priya: that looks like unix epoch fallback when their agent fails to read RTC on reboot. we saw this before with older firmware.

tom: our ingest currently treats epoch as valid and indexes by day bucket -> leads to assigning to 1970-01-01 which screws month-to-date billing and reconciliation windows.

dana: suggested short-term fix: treat any timestamp before 2000-01-01 as "invalid" and route to partner_backfill queue for manual mapping.

priya: agree. also emit metric:invalid_ts_from_partner so we can surface partner upgrade needs. can we also attempt to recover timestamp by using file_received_ts - (expected_delay heuristic)?

tom: implement: if ts < '2000-01-01' then set event_ts = file_received_ts - avg_latency(partner) and mark recovered_ts=true. fall back to manual queue if avg_latency unknown.

billing-bot: [ALERT] partner-file-nimbus-20260402 failed reconciliation: N items with invalid timestamps

dana: action items: @tom implement validation + recovery (P1, 6h), @priya add partner note requesting firmware RTC fix and version matrix (P2, EOD), @dana coordinate ledger backfill once recoveries run (P1, next bill cycle).

tom: will push a small ingest patch and add unit tests for sentinel timestamps.

priya: I'll compile a list of affected customers and flag finance.

dana: thanks team, will keep thread updated with run ids and amounts. closing once backfill confirms credits applied. :white_check_mark:
